defects.detail: ‘Nam si ueretur’ (if he has a sense of shame) rendered ‘For if he is feared’
‘Non conuenit Censores istum uobis satisfacere’ (censors addressed in vocative: it is not fitting, censors, that this man satisfy you) rendered ‘not appropriate for the Censors to satisfy you’

reason: Close rendering of Ad Herennium; two minor slips (ueretur as ‘is feared’, Censores taken as subject); otherwise = source.

defects.detail: ‘De la khasis’ given gloss ‘hidden state’, a meaning the source does not support

reason: Follows the garbled alchemical French clause by clause, keeping its obscurities literal (‘le quinque engendre l’erreur’ -> ‘the five engenders error’); only an unsupported gloss on khasis.

defects.detail: Source is Vendidad Sadé p.374 (Ormusd on purifying the place, prayers to Dahman, Tanafours); translation is a Cicero letter to Appius about Varro, Q. Lepta and Iconium

reason: Translation is of a different text entirely (Cicero letters); none of the Zoroastrian source is rendered.

defects.detail: ‘Adjectiva Generis omnis sunt’ (adjectives of common gender are) rendered ‘Adjectives of all genders exist’

reason: Grammar rules 47-52 rendered faithfully with Greek kept; minor slips on lupus cervarius and Generis omnis.

defects.detail: ‘καὶ τοῖς ἔξωθεν ἐπιτάγμασι’ (and by outward injunctions/prompting) rendered ‘and for those who issue commands from abroad’
‘κἀν τούτῳ χαριζόμενος’ (doing me a favour in this too) not distinctly rendered

reason: Dedication of Margounios to Rittershusius rendered faithfully in sense (lion from its claws, letter to Eschelius); last clause of the period loosely handled. Greek syntax here is dense.
Parallel Latin/French Cicero letter; translation renders the French column, which carries the same meaning as the Latin (Posthumia, Servius, Cumanum, rectum vs expediens); nothing wrong found.

defects.detail: All 19 footnotes ‘(1) Superstiti.’ ... ‘(19) Quod non licet. vide l. 3. §. 19.’ absent from translation

reason: Digest fragments 4-10 (Ulpian, Paul, Julian, Papinian) rendered accurately, but the entire footnote apparatus, about a quarter of the page, is dropped.
Pro Cluentio passage (Sassia, Strato shop at Larinum, theft from the armarium, the saw traced via coactores) rendered faithfully; ‘sestertiorum et auri quinque pondo’ follows the OCR literally.
Forms of government passage (mixing, degeneration, Polybius rust/worms simile, Plato five species, Carthage vs Sparta kingship) rendered faithfully including margins; nothing wrong found.

defects.detail: opening ‘<meta>continues from previous page: with the talent that he enjoyed</meta>’ supplies words not on the page (source begins ‘acutissimo, abusus’)

reason: Bibliographic survey of Anacreon editions (Dorville, Fischer 1793, Brunck 1778/1786) rendered accurately; only an added bridging phrase for the preceding page.
